title: Newborn jaundice: what yellow is OK?
summary: Yellow skin is common in newborns. Most cases are mild and resolve with feeding and time.
whatsNormal:
Jaundice is a yellow tint to skin and eyes from bilirubin, a breakdown product of red blood cells.

• Often appears day 2–4 and peaks around day 5–7 in full-term babies
• Starts on the face and moves down the body as levels rise
• Mild jaundice with good feeding and wet diapers is common
• Gently pressing skin on the nose or chest can show yellow undertone

Frequent feeding helps clear bilirubin through stool. Sunlight through a window is not a substitute for medical follow-up if jaundice is significant.
watchFor: Yellow spreading below the belly button or onto legs and palms
Baby very sleepy, hard to wake for feeds, or not feeding well
Pale or white stools and dark urine
Jaundice that looks worse day to day after day 5 in a full-term baby
callDoctorIf: Yellow skin or eyes in the first 24 hours of life
Baby will not wake for feeds or has fewer wet diapers than expected
Fever, vomiting, or unusual fussiness with jaundice
Your pediatrician or hospital asked you to recheck bilirubin, follow that plan
